The convergence of numerical solutions for rough solutions in C([0, T]; H γ) with an ar-
bitrary small γ > 0 was addressed by Ostermann, Rousset & Schratz [19] and Rousset &
Schratz [24] for the NLS and KdV equations, respectively, by introducing and utilizing the
discrete Bourgain spaces. In particular, for the KdV equation, Rousset & Schratz [24] pro-

The rest of this article is organized as follows. Some basic notations and preliminary results
are presented in Section 2. Several new tools for the construction and analysis of low-regularity
integrators are presented in Section 3, including a logarithmically growing trilinear estimate
on L2, the averaging approximation of exponential functions with imaginary powers, and new
trilinear estimates associated to the KdV operator. The construction of the low-regularity
integrator is presented in Section 4, and the reduction of the proposed numerical scheme to a
continuously formulated perturbed KdV equation is presented in Section 5. The consistency
estimates for the local and global errors are presented in Sections 6 and 7, respectively. The
stability estimates using low- and high-frequency decompositions are presented in Section 8.
The error estimates (i.e., proof of Theorem 1.1), which combine the consistency and stability
estimates, are presented in Section 9. Numerical experiments and conclusions are presented
in Sections 10 and 11, respectively.

11. Conclusions and extended studies
We have presented several new tools for the construction and analysis of low-regularity
integrators for the KdV equations, including the averaging approximation technique for ex-
ponential functions with imaginary powers (Lemma 3.2), the new estimates for the symbol
ϕ = k3 − k3
1 − k3
2 − k3
3 (Lemma 3.3), and new trilinear estimates associated to the KdV op-
erator (Proposition 3.4). These new techniques have played essential roles in analyzing the
local error, global remainder, and the stability estimates. We have also introduced a new
technique, which reformulates the numerical scheme into a perturbed integral formulation of
the continuous KdV equation globally posed on the time interval [0 , T], instead of locally
posed on [tn, tn+1], for analyzing the stability of numerical approximations to solutions below
H 1. By combining the several new techniques, we have constructed a new time discretiza-
tion which is convergent with order γ in L2 (up to a logarithmic factor) under the regularity
condition u ∈ C([0, T]; H γ), with γ ∈ (0, 1] possibly approaching zero.
This paper focuses on the development of low-regularity integrators that could improve
the convergence rates of time discretization without the necessity of using filters. Typically,
filters necessitates a stepsize that correlates with the degrees of freedom in space discretization,
similar to a CFL condition. Our approach increases the flexibility in choosing the degrees of
freedom for space discretization, which enables the design of a fully discrete numerical scheme
that operates independently of any CFL condition. We believe that rigorous analysis of the
full discretization, when coupled with the Fourier spectral method in space, can be conducted
within the theoretical framework proposed in this paper, which provides a foundation for such
future research.
The algorithm constructed in this paper improves the error from O(τ γ/3) to O(τ γ ln(1/τ )),
with a logarithmic factor ln(1 /τ ) arising from technical estimates detailed within our paper.
The optimality of the logarithmic factor ln(1 /τ ) is uncertain since the numerical tests cannot
reveal the logarithmic influence on convergence rates. Typically, if the theoretical error is
expressed as O(τ γ−ϵ) for any ϵ in the range (0 , γ), numerical tests would generally reflect a
convergence order of γ. Hence, further study is required to determine if the logarithmic term
can be refined in future analyses.
The methodologies and theoretical framework introduced in this article can be extended
to develop low-regularity integrators for a variety of nonlinear dispersive equations. These in-
clude the modified KdV equation, the generalized KdV equation, and the nonlinear Schr¨ odinger
(NLS) equation. For instance, consider the NLS equation given by

2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization and supplied core proof route. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | Verify the actual AND dependency graph, unique producers, absence of cycles and faithful exported statements. Retain every original H and disclose unused H. Internal results are proved, never new roots. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Inputs and output state the mathematical content, objects, domains, quantifiers and conditions their consumers need. Check actual object occurrences and definitions. No missing identification can be supplied by an absent producer proof or a paper equation number. |
21: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Check direct input use, earlier local facts, witness existence and proper discharge of assumptions. No circular dependency, future fact or escaped local object is allowed. Mathematically checked routine background may supplement the packet without prior native lookup. |
22: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Verify the complete implication and every output clause at ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity, including material limiting operations, domains and regularity. Compress correct routine reasoning; locate a real gap rather than requiring a transcript of elementary steps. |
23: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | Check actual instantiations and all material premises of invoked E/M or routine background facts, with grounds in inputs or earlier local derivations. Required bridges are proved. A familiar theorem name or a proposed Lean tactic supplies no mathematical justification. |
24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.
86: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
87: 
88: ## Execution protocol
89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Up to the explicitly confirmed N independent R reviewers work concurrently.
96:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
97:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
98: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
99:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
100:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
101:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
102: 4. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
103:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
104:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
105:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
106:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
107:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
108: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
109:    structure_review and findings. Each E adds citation_checks for
110:    literature_identity, result_location, statement_fidelity,
111:    context_completeness, version_and_eligibility. Inaccessible primary text
112:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.
113: 6. A blocking finding needs its actual location, explanation and a short exact
114:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
115:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
116:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
117: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
118:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
119:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
120:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
121: 
122: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
123: 
124: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
125: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
126: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
127: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
128: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
129: 
130: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
131: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.
132: The ordinary complete result remains relative to explicit E assumptions.
133: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation
134: retains this exact audit and supplement until reviewed mathematical changes
135: invalidate affected scopes. Typed interfaces, native checking, standalone
136: assembly and independent semantic Audit B are separate later gates.

141: secondary statement and actual access evidence; unavailable source checks
142: stay UNVERIFIED. Continue other work only with an explicitly qualified source
143: assumption, and report warn.json/warn.md. No unqualified full PASS is granted."}

in H s; see [1,10,12,33]. However, classical time discretizations for the KdV equation, including

    Title:On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation

    Authors:Anatoli V. Babin, Alexei A. Ilyin, Edriss S. Titi
            View a PDF of the paper titled On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation, by Anatoli V. Babin and 1 other authors

    View PDF
    HTML (experimental)



    
            Abstract:In this paper we develop and use successive averaging methods for explaining the regularization mechanism in the the periodic Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in the homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\dot{H}^s$, for $s\ge0$. Specifically, we prove the global existence, uniqueness, and Lipschitz continuous dependence on the initial data of the solutions of the periodic KdV. For the case where the initial data is in $L_2$ we also show the Lipschitz continuous dependence of these solutions with respect to the initial data as maps from $\dot{H}^s$ to $\dot{H}^s$, for $s\in(-1,0]$.

    Title:On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation

    Authors:Anatoli V. Babin, Alexei A. Ilyin, Edriss S. Titi
            View a PDF of the paper titled On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation, by Anatoli V. Babin and 1 other authors

    View PDF
    HTML (experimental)



    
            Abstract:In this paper we develop and use successive averaging methods for explaining the regularization mechanism in the the periodic Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in the homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\dot{H}^s$, for $s\ge0$. Specifically, we prove the global existence, uniqueness, and Lipschitz continuous dependence on the initial data of the solutions of the periodic KdV. For the case where the initial data is in $L_2$ we also show the Lipschitz continuous dependence of these solutions with respect to the initial data as maps from $\dot{H}^s$ to $\dot{H}^s$, for $s\in(-1,0]$.

spec.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u and the fixed unfiltered scheme U defined below satisfy max_{0<=n<=L} ||u(n*tau)-U^n||_2 <= C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. Both constants are uniform over the entire initial-data ball, all such L, and Fourier support.

definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

definitions.type: family of real or complex Hilbert spaces indexed by real order
definitions.definition: Write <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_{k in Z}<k>^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2, interpreted as distributions for s<0. L^2=H^0 and ||.||_2 denotes its normalized norm. For mean-zero f, ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2. For s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s). In time L^infty norms are essential suprema, replaced by ordinary suprema for continuous representatives; derivative norms remain essential suprema.

definitions.type: one-parameter family of linear Fourier operators
definitions.definition: For real t, S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3) has Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3).
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at zero. Write Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). Spatial differentiation partial_x has multiplier i*k.

definitions.type: family of time-step maps and finite trajectories
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, define Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2]. Define Htau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets are upper endpoint minus lower endpoint and products are spatial products. Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f). For a positive integer L, tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau; U^0=u0, U^(n+1)=Psi_tau(U^n), 0<=n<L. This is the unmodified scheme with no frequency cutoff. Its elementary L^2 well-definedness and continuity are proved below.
For real K>=0, P_(<=K) has multiplier 1_(|k|<=K) and P_(>K)=I-P_(<=K). These are proof devices and are absent from Scheme.

definitions.type: averaged covariance of two real phases
definitions.definition: For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
For integers a,b,c and k=a+b+c, set p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3.

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, resolving ties in any order. Nthird(a,b,c,d)=N3. Thus N3 is the second smallest of all four magnitudes including the dual output.

definitions.type: family of trilinear Fourier operators initially on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, real base time t_n and k!=0, hat R2_(t_n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)(k)=-(tau/(18*i*k))*sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0}exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with zero coefficient at k=0; Phase gives alpha,beta,Phi. Write R2^n_tau for t_n=n*tau. Bounded extensions, when used, are proved below.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)]. Initially use smooth inputs; the negative Sobolev extension to L^2 inputs is proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For I=[a,b], C_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt. Constant inputs are identified with constant time paths. At smooth inputs this is an ordinary integral, and the source estimates supply its continuous extensions.

definitions.type: norm on time paths with weak derivative
definitions.definition: For an interval I, ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infty(I;L^2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-pstar))). Use the continuous L^2 representative wherever supplied.

definitions.type: family of bilinear integrated quadratic stages
definitions.definition: For a base time a>=0, step tau>0, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero inputs f,g, F_a(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(f,g)ds. Abbreviate F_a(t;f)=F_a(t;f,f). Its endpoint representation and extensions are proved below.

definitions.type: distributional evolution equation and smooth-approximation solution convention
definitions.definition: KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0, with real mean-zero data on Torus. An exact solution at regularity sigma>=0 means its unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^sigma) distributional solution obtained as the limit of smooth-data solutions. This convention alone grants neither existence nor a bound; these are proved from the registered flow source. For an existing solution write its twisted path v(t)=S_(-t)u(t).

definitions.type: stepwise interpolation and residual construction from a smooth trajectory
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t_n=n*tau, and a finite smooth mean-zero trajectory f_n, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put F_n(t)=F_(t_n)(t;f_n,f_n), z_n=f_n+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f_n,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n, and Y_n=V-z_n. Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n. The residual path mathcalR is the concatenation of these increments: mathcalR(0)=0 and mathcalR(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. This construction does not assert endpoint compatibility; that is proved when f_n are the twisted Scheme trajectory.

propositions.statement: Source flow assertions on the normalized 2*pi torus, in mean-zero homogeneous spaces: for real mean-zero initial datum q, define U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx and its twist y_k(t)=exp(i*t*k^3)hat U(t,k), satisfying y'_k=(i*k/2)sum_{r+s=k}exp(3*i*k*r*s*t)y_r*y_s. (i) For sigma>=0, horizon b>0, and ||q||_2<=B0, the Galerkin approximations with nonlinearity projected onto |k|<=m are uniformly bounded in L^infty([0,b];dot H^sigma) by A_sigma depending only on sigma,b,B0,||q||_(dot H^sigma) (bound clause of Theorem 4.2). (ii) If sigma>0 and 0<rho<sigma, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];H^rho), every fixed 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infty dot H^sigma to a coefficientwise integral solution with the same bound and ||y(t)||_2=||q||_2 a.e. (Theorem 4.3). source.context: Sections 1-2 and 3.3: 2*pi-periodic functions, coefficients normalized by 1/(2*pi) but function norms use unnormalized dx; P deletes zero mode. Interval endpoints nonnegative, length bounded by a fixed constant. Source estimates are uniform in time level, timestep and spectral support. The source convergence theorem is not imported.
source.qualification: Proved assertions in an identifiable primary research text; only the explicitly stated source clauses are imported, with every condition and parameter range retained. Project estimates and normalization/sign bridges remain internal.

Primary results and scheme were compared in this manuscript, without substituting journal equation numbering. hypotheses: tau>0, t_n=n*tau>=0, and f is a smooth mean-zero periodic input.
The update is the exact source scheme (1.4), with no cutoff, transformed by v^n=S_(-t_n)U^n.

propositions.statement: For every real mean-zero q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R, KdV has the exact solution prescribed in D020; it belongs to C([0,T];H^gamma), and sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity uniformly in q. For smooth q the solution is smooth. The twist v=S_(-t)u has the same norms and satisfies v'=B_t(v,v)/2. For any two such solutions with initial L^2 norms summing to at most B0, sup_[0,T]||u-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-qtilde||_2. In particular smooth approximations with bounded H^gamma norm converge in C([0,T];L^2); M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma) is bounded by 1+A(T,gamma,R).
propositions.origin: problem.md:105-122; sign and homogeneous/inhomogeneous norm bridge.

propositions.statement: For all I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and h=b-a<=1, all 0<=sigma<=1 and paths f_j in L^infty(I;H^sigma) with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-pstar)), Ctri satisfies ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C*||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))*product_{j!=i}||f_j||_(L^infty L^2), each i=1,2,3. For time-independent inputs, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*h^sigma*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), including sigma=0. For 0<sigma<=1 choose a_sigma=1/2-sigma for sigma<1/2, a_sigma=1/8 for sigma=1/2, a_sigma=0 for sigma>1/2. Then 0<=a_sigma<1 and ||fg||_2<=C_sigma||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^a_sigma). For any constant mean-zero w in H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and a>=0, sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^a_sigma)<=C_(M,sigma)*tau^sigma and sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^(1+sigma))<=C_(M,sigma). All these are in the normalized norms, with constants uniform in endpoints and support.
propositions.origin: problem.md:334-369; explicit source normalization and stage-exponent specialization.

propositions.statement: For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|). For every nonzero integer quadruple a+b+c+d=0, N1<=3*N2 and, writing A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, one has (1/|d|)*min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/Nthird(a,b,c,d), and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/Nthird(a,b,c,d).
propositions.origin: problem.md:145-203; covariance and pointwise four-frequency majorants.

propositions.statement: There is an absolute C such that for all nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_{a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0} x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_{j=1}^4||xj||_(ell^2). The sum is the supremum of finite positive partial sums; the same bound holds when it is restricted to any subset of quadruples.
propositions.origin: problem.md:204-251; dyadic summation with geometric smaller-scale gain.

propositions.statement: For 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, any real base time a, and mean-zero fj in H^sigma, ||R2_(a,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly in a,tau and Fourier support. The bound holds after inserting any multiplier of modulus <=1, including restriction to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. Polynomial approximation defines its unique continuous trilinear extension. Moreover, for 0<gamma<=1, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f in mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(a,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). This estimate requires no H^gamma bound on f.
propositions.origin: problem.md:253-299; mixed remainder theorem including exponent zero and numerical-state corollary.

propositions.statement: For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. H^1 is an algebra: ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

propositions.origin: problem.md:315-333,370-398; local Fourier product bounds and exact normal forms.

propositions.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau from Scheme is a continuous polynomial map from mean-zero L^2 to mean-zero L^2, preserving reality; Ftau maps L^2 continuously to H^1. Smooth data produce smooth iterates. For any smooth trajectory produced by Scheme, f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, the Interp construction has V(t_n)=f_n, V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), is continuous and piecewise smooth in time and spatially smooth, and has real mean-zero values. On each open step, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+mathcalR', where mathcalR'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. Thus mathcalR is continuous with the defining increments and the displayed residual identity holds a.e.
propositions.origin: problem.md:399-431,501-514,632-641; source scheme bridge and elementary well-definedness.

propositions.statement: Let 0<tau<=1, let u be a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution on [0,T], v=S_(-t)u, and M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma). On any step of the smooth twisted Scheme trajectory f_n, assume delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 and put q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. For Interp, with constants C_M depending only on M,gamma,T, uniformly in n,tau and support: sup_(I_n)||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, sup_(I_n)||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;v(t_n))||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta_n; sup_(I_n)(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q_n; ||z_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M; sup_(I_n)||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv B_t(f_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q_n, ||Y_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n. Here a_gamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, 1/8 if gamma=1/2, and 0 if gamma>1/2. No numerical H^gamma norm is used.
propositions.origin: problem.md:432-499; stage, endpoint correction, interpolation defect and weak smallness.

propositions.statement: Under the step assumptions of N008 (explicitly: smooth exact solution with twisted H^gamma size <=M-1, smooth numerical trajectory, 0<tau<=1, delta_n<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n), Interp satisfies sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*q_n. On any I=[a,b] contained in [0,T] with a a grid point, h=b-a<=1, define e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2. If E_I<=1 then sup_I||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_M. Intervals may end inside a step; derivative assertions hold a.e.
propositions.origin: problem.md:501-540; stepwise residual calculation and accumulated interval estimates.

propositions.statement: For smooth exact/numerical paths of N007-N009, M>=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, every grid-start interval I=[a,b] of length h<=1 with E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1 and every real N>=2 satisfy E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, where e=v-V. The constant depends only on M,gamma,T, not a,b,N,tau,support, and the interval may end inside a step. Both normal-form endpoints are retained.
propositions.origin: problem.md:543-614; low/high decomposition with exact forcing normal form.

propositions.statement: There exist positive C and tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero datum q with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, its exact solution and the unmodified Scheme satisfy sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C*tau^gamma for Interp built from its twisted numerical trajectory. In particular max_(0<=n<=L)||u(t_n)-U^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The constants are independent of higher Sobolev norms and spectral support.
propositions.origin: problem.md:615-631; restarted finite-block recurrence and continuity bootstrap.

Take the unique source solution with initial datum -q(-x), supplied by E001 under L1.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary datum q and assume L1: q is real and mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma, and ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1, R>0. Reflection with a minus sign sends q to -q(-x) without changing any Fourier Sobolev norm. Apply E001's positive-regularity existence and uniqueness clauses at sigma=gamma, horizon T, and initial L^2 bound R; at smooth data apply them at every higher order as well, and uniqueness identifies these solutions. Its homogeneous bounds transfer to the inhomogeneous norms because 1<=<k>/|k|<=sqrt(2) for k!=0. Thus the source solutions have a common H^gamma bound depending only on T,gamma,R. E001's bound can equivalently be taken uniformly on the initial norm ball as stated in its bound clause.

produces.statement: The source flow for -q(-x) exists, is unique and continuous at order gamma, and has an H^gamma bound A(T,gamma,R); smooth q gives smooth flow.

argument.text: Set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). At (t,-x), u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx, so u_t+u_xxx=-U*U_x=u*u_x. Also hat u(k)=-hat U(-k), preserving reality, mean and all norms. The initial datum is q. Reflection is an involution, so source uniqueness transfers. The source coefficientwise integrated equation becomes distributional KdV under this change: products of L^2 functions are L^1, and each tested Fourier coefficient is absolutely integrable in time. Twisting by S_(-t) removes the linear term and gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Unitarity follows directly from the modulus-one multiplier; hence M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A(T,gamma,R).

produces.statement: u is the required unique KdV flow and v'=B_t(v,v)/2, with the uniform H^gamma bound and smoothness asserted in N001.

argument.text: For any two such initial data with L^2 norms summing to B0 or less, apply E001(iv) at theta=0 and horizon T to their reflected data. Twisting and reflection preserve the L^2 distance, giving sup||u-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-qtilde||_2. In particular the real mean-zero Fourier truncations of q converge to q in H^gamma and L^2, stay in the same norm ball, and their flows converge uniformly in L^2; uniqueness identifies the limit with the flow just constructed. Thus this is exactly the prescribed smooth-approximation solution. The uniform H^gamma bound also passes to the limit by taking limits in every finite nonnegative Fourier norm sum and then their supremum. Discharge L1 and quantify q and the two-flow assertion; this proves every clause of N001.

applications.bindings: Use sigma=gamma, b=T, q_source(x)=-q(-x), B0=R; for smooth q also use each higher sigma.
hypothesis_checks: L1 and reflection give real mean-zero source data on Torus; H001 gives T>0.
H002 and L1 supply the positive order and finite homogeneous norms, bounded by the inhomogeneous ones; smooth q has every order.
The initial L^2 norm is <=R by L1; the two-flow clause is not used in this application.

applications.bindings: Use clause (iv) with theta=0, b=T, bound B0 equal to any upper bound on the two initial L^2 norms, and the two reflected source flows.
hypothesis_checks: The two compared flows have real mean-zero data; H001 and the preceding construction give the horizon and source solutions.
The data and solutions in F002 are at positive order, hence in dot H^0; theta=0 is an allowed endpoint.
The comparison is explicitly conditional on the sum of initial L^2 norms being <=B0; theta=0 lies in (-1,0].

argument.text: First apply E002 to arbitrary qualifying paths on I=[a,b], h=b-a<=1, using alpha=sigma. The source function norms all equal sqrt(2*pi) times the normalized norms, including both components of X. Dividing a cubic estimate by sqrt(2*pi) leaves the fixed factor 2*pi in its constant. Its C operator has precisely the same Fourier coefficients, means and inverse derivatives as Ctri; therefore both trilinear estimates, all three choices of negative slot, and both exponent endpoints hold as stated in N002. This is a universally quantified conditional application, with exactly E002's interval, path and constant-input conditions retained.

produces.statement: Both normalized Ctri estimates of N002 hold with all of their stated interval and regularity conditions.

argument.text: Now fix sigma,tau,a,w,M and assume L1: 0<sigma<=1, 0<tau<=1, a>=0, w is constant mean-zero H^sigma and ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M. Choose a_sigma=1/2-sigma,1/8,0 in the three indicated ranges. E004 with this fixed 1/8 loss proves the asserted product estimate; division by sqrt(2*pi) again changes only the constant. Put beta0=2*sigma-3/2, -5/8, sigma-1 respectively. Every a_sigma lies in [beta0,1+sigma]. At beta=a_sigma the source E003 exponents are (1/2+2*sigma)/(5/2-sigma), 11/17, and (1+sigma)/2 respectively. The first is >=sigma since sigma^2-sigma/2+1/2>0; the middle exceeds 1/2, and the last is >=sigma since sigma<=1. At beta=1+sigma the exponent is zero.

produces.statement: Under L1, the product inequality holds, the two selected beta values are allowed, and the source stage exponents at a_sigma and 1+sigma are at least sigma and zero, respectively.

argument.text: Apply E003 at those two beta values, with both inputs w. Since 0<tau<=1 and the exponent at a_sigma is >=sigma, tau^theta<=tau^sigma. The resulting bounds are C_sigma*M^2*tau^sigma and C_sigma*M^2. Converting the norms multiplies constants only by fixed powers of sqrt(2*pi). This proves the two uniform stage bounds. Together with F001 and the product bound, discharge L1 and quantify all selected data. No assertion about the numerical trajectory's Sobolev norm has been imported.

argument.text: Fix tau,alpha,beta and assume L1: tau>0. If either phase is zero, eta=0 by the definition. Otherwise set h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)); then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha|*|s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau|alpha|*|s-r|dr<=tau*|alpha|. Therefore |eta|<=tau*|alpha|, and symmetry gives tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|).

produces.statement: For tau>0, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|), and it vanishes if alpha*beta=0.

argument.text: More sharply, |h(0)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 and |h(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 by integrating r and tau-r. Also integral_0^tau |h'(s)|ds=tau*|alpha|. Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s) thus gives |eta|<=(|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau*|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta|. Interchanging alpha,beta proves the minimum of the two ratios. The zero-phase case already settled extends the result without dividing by zero. Discharge L1.

For the frequency assertion fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L2: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. The triangle inequality gives N1<=3*N2. Put A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. If d is among the largest two, min(A/B0,B0/A)/|d|<=1/N3. Otherwise the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, bound the minimum by B0/A and obtain |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio is between 1/3 and 3; the remaining sizes |b|,|d| have maximum N3. Hence the expression is <=3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3. The b,c case is identical after exchanging a,b. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily and these alternatives still cover them.

produces.statement: Under L2, N1<=3*N2 and min(A/B0,B0/A)/|d|<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, use the pairing (a,b),(c,d). If the largest two are in the same pair, the other pair has sum <=2*N3, while max(A,B0)>=N1*N2. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If the largest two are in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, so max(A,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2. The quotient is <=6/N3. Discharge L2 and universally quantify; together with the first two paragraphs this proves N003.

Fix x2 as specified in this proof.
Fix x3 as specified in this proof.
Fix x4 as specified in this proof.
For r=1,2,3,4 define Xshell_(r,j)=||x_r 1_(2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1))||_ell2, j>=0, extended by zero at negative j.
Fix q as specified in this proof.
Fix m as specified in this proof.

argument.text: Fix four sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 and assume L1: they are nonnegative and in ell^2(Z\{0}). First truncate to finite support. Partition the nonzero integers into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be the corresponding ell^2 norm. Sum over the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices; relabel the sequence positions within one ordering so j1>=j2>=j3>=j4. The zero-sum relation implies the largest frequency <=3 times the second largest, hence j1-j2<=2. For each fixed pair of frequencies in the smaller shells, the sum over the remaining two with prescribed sum is at most the product of their ell^2 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz (a translated reflection preserves the norm). Each smaller shell has <=2^(j+1) integers. Taking their ell^1 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz gives a shell contribution <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). Dividing by Nthird>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr).

produces.statement: For each ordered interacting shell tuple, 0<=j1-j2<=2 and the weighted shell contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr).

argument.text: For q=j1-j2 in {0,1,2}, drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shell indices in this nonnegative sum. The resulting bound factors as C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)Xshell_(3,ell)Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is <=||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. In the second, write r=ell-m and apply Cauchy-Schwarz for each r; it is <=sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell orthogonality gives ||Xshell_r||_ell2=||x_r||_ell2. Summing the 24 orderings and three offsets proves the finite-support inequality with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: The asserted four-linear inequality holds with one absolute constant for all finite-support nonnegative inputs.

argument.text: For general inputs apply F002 to x_r restricted to |k|<=m and let m tend to infinity. Each norm is bounded by the full ell^2 norm. Every finite set of contributing quadruples is included at some m, and the nonnegative infinite sum is defined as the supremum of those finite sums. Therefore the same bound holds without exchanging conditionally convergent series. Restricting to any subset decreases a nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 and quantify the four inputs; this proves N004.

Set delta=||f-w||_2.

argument.text: Fix sigma,tau,a0,f1,f2,f3 and assume L1: 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, and each f_j is mean-zero in H^sigma. Initially take polynomial inputs. In a nonzero term set k=a+b+c, p=a+b and d=-k. Terms with a zero input, k=0 or p=0 vanish or are excluded; if a phase is zero eta vanishes. For the remaining terms set A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, so the ratio of |alpha| and |beta| is the ratio of A and B0. N003 therefore gives |eta|/|k|<=6/Nthird. Its other covariance bound gives |eta|/(tau*|abck|)<=3*|p|*min(A,B0)/(A*B0)=3*|p|/max(A,B0)<=18/Nthird. Interpolating these two numerical inequalities with powers 1-sigma and sigma gives |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird. All constants here are independent of the base time.

produces.statement: Under L1 the remainder multiplier obeys |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird(a,b,c,-k) on every contributing term.

argument.text: Dualize the R2 Fourier sum against any finitely supported ell^2 sequence of norm one and take absolute values. Use N004 with x1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f1(a)|, x2(b)=|b|^sigma|hat f2(b)|, x3(c)=|c|^sigma|hat f3(c)| and x4(d)=the absolute value of the dual coefficient at -d. The first three ell^2 norms are bounded by the H^sigma norms. The factors exp(-i*a0*Phi) have modulus one. With the prefactor tau/18, F001 and N004 give C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product||fj||_(H^sigma). The same absolute-envelope argument allows any inserted multiplier of modulus <=1 and any subset of frequencies, including either total-phase restriction.

produces.statement: Under L1 the full and modulus-one-restricted R2 estimates in N005 hold for polynomial inputs, including sigma=0.

argument.text: Approximate each input by its Fourier truncations in H^sigma. Trilinearity and F002 bound every telescoping difference by a sum of one vanishing norm times two bounded norms. Thus the outputs are Cauchy in complete L^2, independent of the approximations, and define the claimed continuous extension and bound. At nonzero fixed output the coefficient is the same continuous limit of the polynomial formula. Discharge L1 and quantify these inputs.

produces.statement: For every 0<=sigma<=1 and all inputs in H^sigma the R2 estimate and its continuous trilinear extension hold, including arbitrary bounded multiplier restrictions.

argument.text: For the numerical-state assertion fix w,f,M and assume L2: w is mean-zero H^gamma, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f is mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1. H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Apply F003 at sigma=gamma to (w,w,w). Expand the difference at (f,f,f) by trilinearity, for example R2(f-w,f,f)+R2(w,f-w,f)+R2(w,w,f-w), and use F003 at sigma=0 in every term. Since ||f||_2<=M+1, the difference is <=C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Adding the exact-data bound gives C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). Discharge L2 and quantify; no numerical Sobolev norm entered.

argument.text: For arbitrary mean-zero L^2 input f, Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. More generally H^1 embeds into L^infty by the summability of <k>^(-2). For A,A2 in H^1, ||AA2||_2<=||A||_infinity||A2||_2 and partial_x(AA2)=A' A2+A A2', giving ||AA2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). These first hold for polynomials and extend by completeness. Since S_t is an isometry on H^s by its modulus-one multiplier, this proves ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. S_t also preserves reality and zero mode. Strong continuity follows by dominated convergence in the weighted square-summable Fourier series.

produces.statement: The inverse derivative estimates, H^1 algebra inequality, J_t H^1 bound, and all stated S_t properties hold.

argument.text: For L^2 functions F,G, the convolution coefficient satisfies |hat(FG)(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2. Thus ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2*sum_(k!=0)k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), which is finite since pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound and sum k^(-2)<infinity give ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1) gives ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. Finally, in J_t(A,g), bound S_t Dinv A in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infty using F001, proving the asymmetric estimate. These bounds justify the stated bounded extensions by polynomial density.

produces.statement: The negative-Sobolev B bound, inverse derivative of a product bound, weak norm comparison and asymmetric J bound hold uniformly in time.

argument.text: Now fix arbitrary piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b] and a third such path h. On k!=0 the coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(r+s=k)exp(-3*i*k*r*s*t)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiation of the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients, so d_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smoothness gives absolute Fourier convergence for every derivative used. Integrate and divide by three to obtain the normal form, summing over pieces if necessary; continuity makes the internal endpoints cancel. Symmetry is immediate. Because Dinv partial_x=P and S_t commutes with these Fourier multipliers, J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}. Integrating gives C_I(f,g,h) with no commutation through a product. At constant f,g the derivative terms vanish, giving Stage=[J]_a^t/6. Quantifying the inputs proves N006.

argument.text: For fixed tau>0, N006 gives Dinv:L^2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound. Thus Ftau is a continuous quadratic L^2->H^1 map. The first Htau term is a product of two inverse derivatives followed by P. The second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2. The third has an H^1 cubic product followed by Dinv. The fourth has Dinv2 Ftau(f) and Dinv f, again an H^1 product followed by Dinv2; all coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for fixed tau. Hence Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L^2 to L^2. Every output is mean-zero: the first and third/fourth corrections have P or an inverse derivative; the mean of the second term is zero because Dinv f has zero mean. Conjugate Fourier symmetry and the real coefficients give reality. Smoothness is preserved by these operations, so finite smooth trajectories exist without any bound on their higher norms.

produces.statement: At each fixed positive tau the displayed Scheme is a continuous real mean-zero L^2 map and preserves smoothness.

argument.text: For any smooth input f at grid step n, identify source exp(t*partial_x^3) with S_(-t). The source Ftau,Htau formulas are exactly D008, term by term, with coefficients 1/6,1/3,tau/9,-1/54,-1/(27*tau), and identical endpoint signs. The source inverse derivative and mean have the same multipliers. In the twist, S_(-(t_n+tau))Ftau(S_(t_n)f)=F_(t_n)(t_n+tau;f,f), also following from N006's endpoint formula. The source cubic remainder has alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b), the covariance eta and the prefactor -tau/(18ik), exactly R2. E005 therefore yields f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2^n_tau(f_n,f_n,f_n). Substitution in Interp makes Q_n(t_(n+1)) cancel with its part of W_n; hence V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1).

produces.statement: For smooth Scheme trajectories the interpolation matches both step endpoints and the source remainder is exactly R2, with the sign in D021.

argument.text: Endpoint matching gives continuity across all grid points; all ingredients are spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth. On a step F_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, C_n'=B_t(f_n,F_n), Q_n'=B_t(F_n,F_n)/2. Thus V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. Since V=z_n+Y_n, expansion gives V'=B_t(V,V)/2-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. The last three terms are precisely rho_n' and hence mathcalR' on that step. The concatenation is continuous at its endpoints and starts at zero. The mean and reality properties follow from F001 and the real, mean-zero operators used throughout. Quantify the smooth trajectory and fixed tau to obtain N007.

applications.bindings: Source vn=f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, source F^n=F_(t_n) from Stage, source A^n=C_n(t_(n+1)), source R2^n=R2_(t_n,tau). Source scheme (1.4)=D008.
hypothesis_checks: The paragraph considers a smooth mean-zero f_n, at tau>0 and n>=0; F001 ensures such Scheme iterates exist.
The termwise comparison of the fixed update and the Airy twist identifies the exact source scheme, with no cutoff or convergence assumption.

locals.declaration: Fix tau as specified in this proof.
Fix u as specified in this proof.
Fix v as specified in this proof.
Fix M as specified in this proof.
Fix n as specified in this proof.
Set f=f_n, the twisted numerical value on this step.
Set w=v(t_n).
Set delta=||f-w||_2.
Set q=tau^gamma+delta.
Set A(t)=F_(t_n)(t;w,w).
Set D(t)=F_n(t)-A(t).

argument.text: Fix a smooth exact solution and a smooth numerical trajectory, a step n and M, and assume L1: 0<tau<=1, M>=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with f=f_n and w=v(t_n). Put q=tau^gamma+delta<=2. H002 gives the positive gamma range. In particular ||f||_2<=M and ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M. By N006, F_n(t)=[J_s(f,f)]_(t_n)^t/6, so sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M. Bilinearity of J gives sup||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;w,w)||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta. N002 gives the exact-data stage bound in H^a_gamma; since a_gamma<1 the H^1 difference controls this weaker norm. Consequently sup(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q. Also z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2 and N006 imply ||z_n||_X<=C_M.

produces.statement: Under L1 all the F_n stage estimates and ||z_n||_X<=C_M asserted in N008 hold; q<=2.

argument.text: Write A=F_(t_n)(t;w,w), D=F_n-A. For the exact-data square, N002's product estimate with f=partial_x(S_t A), g=S_t A gives ||partial_x[(S_t A)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||A||_(H^(1+gamma))||A||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M*tau^gamma. For the difference of squares, (S_t F_n)^2-(S_t A)^2=(S_t D)*S_t(F_n+A). The H^1 algebra inequality of N006, F001, and ||D||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta bound its derivative by C_M*delta. Thus sup||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q. Integration gives sup||Q_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. N005 applied to f and w gives ||R2^n_tau(f,f,f)||_2<=C_M*tau*q, hence ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 sup||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q and sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

argument.text: The exact formula Dinv B_t(f,F_n)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F_n)] splits into the w product and the (f-w) product. By N002 and F001 the first is <=C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M*q. The second is <=||f-w||_2||S_t F_n||_infinity<=C_M*delta by N006 and the uniform H^1 stage bound. Therefore sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q. Now Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau. F002, boundedness of Dinv on mean-zero L^2, and integration from Y_n(t_n)=0 yield sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q and sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 the Dinv B bound and both Dinv Y_n and Dinv Y_n' bounds in N008 hold.

argument.text: For the strong Y_n bound apply N006's normal form to C_n(t)=integral B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, using F_n(t_n)=0 and F_n'=B_s(f,f)/2. Symmetry of J and its cubic identity give exactly C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-C_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6. The first term is O_M(q) in L^2 by N006 and F001. For the second use N002's constant-input estimate at exponent gamma on (w,w,w); expand its difference from (f,f,f) by trilinearity and use N002 at exponent zero, with ||f-w||_2=delta and ||f||_2+||w||_2<=2M. The result is C_M*(tau^gamma+delta)=C_M*q. Combining with Y_n=C_n+Q_n-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n and F002 proves sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q, with the exact normal form C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-C_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6.

argument.text: Because pstar>1, N006's mean-zero weak-norm comparison and F003 give sup||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q and sup||Y_n'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*q. Together with F004 these give ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q. All constants depended only on the displayed low norms, gamma and the fixed horizon; no higher norm of f was used. Discharge L1 and quantify the data and step, yielding N008.

argument.text: Assume L1: the step hypotheses of N008 hold, with q=tau^gamma+delta_n<=2. In rho_n's first integral apply N006's normal form to B(Y_n,z_n). The boundary J(Y_n,z_n) is O_M(tau*q) by N008's Dinv Y_n bound and N006's asymmetric J bound. The integral J(Y_n',z_n) is also O_M(tau*q) by the Dinv Y_n' bound and ||z_n||_2<=C_M. Since z_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, the remaining integral is C(f_n,f_n,Y_n)/2 by N006. Apply N002's variable-path estimate with the negative slot on Y_n: its X norm is O_M(q), its negative norm is O_M(tau*q), and the constant f_n paths have bounded X and L^2 norms. Thus this integral is O_M(tau*q), for every partial step as well.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(I_n)||integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

argument.text: For the second integral in rho_n apply the same normal form with Y_n in both slots. Its boundary is bounded by ||Dinv Y_n||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2; its derivative integral is bounded by tau*||Dinv Y_n'||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2. Since q<=2, these are O_M(tau*q). The endpoint correction is bounded by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. N007 gives mathcalR'=-B(Y_n,z_n)-B(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. N006's negative-norm product bound and N008 give ||mathcalR'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(q+q^2+q)<=C_M*q. Discharge L1, retaining the fully quantified step estimates.

produces.statement: Every qualifying step has sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*(tau^gamma+delta_n) and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+delta_n).

argument.text: Now fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, and assume L2: e=v-V has E_I<=1, with the smooth paths and M bound as stated in N009. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps, and at every such step start delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. Summing F002's completed increments plus its valid partial-step bound gives sup||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also v'=B_t(v,v)/2, so N006 bounds ||v||_X by C_M. From e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-mathcalR', ||e||_2<=E_I, ||v||_2<=M and the derivative part of F002 we obtain ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I). Hence ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and V=v-e gives ||V||_X<=C_M. Discharge L2 and quantify. The a.e. step derivatives and continuous concatenations give exactly N009 on arbitrary such intervals.

Fix N as specified in this proof.

Set Fint(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,g)ds.
Set Lcut=P_(<=N/3).
Set Hcut=I-Lcut.

argument.text: Fix the smooth paths and I=[a,b], threshold N, step tau and size M, and assume L1: I starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, M>=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, N>=2. Put g=v-e/2 and Fint(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,g)ds. N007 and the exact equation give e(t)=e(a)+Fint(t)-(mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)). For low frequencies, N006 gives ||Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]||_2<=C||e||_2||g||_2. Applying two spatial derivatives on |k|<=N bounds ||P_(<=N)B_s(e,g)||_2 by C_M*N^2*E_I, since S_s is unitary and ||g||_2<=M+1. Integration gives sup||P_(<=N)Fint||_2<=C_M*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact error identity and low-output bound sup||P_(<=N)Fint||_2<=C_M*N^2*h*E_I hold.

argument.text: Use N006's normal form, retaining both endpoints, together with e'=B(e,g)-mathcalR' and g'=B(v,v)/2-B(e,g)/2+mathcalR'/2. In the differentiated J terms, symmetry gives C(e,g,g)-C(e,g,e)/2=C(e,g,V), because g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is C(v,v,e)/2. The forcing terms combine as -J(mathcalR',g)+J(e,mathcalR')/2=-J(mathcalR',V). Therefore exactly Fint(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/3-C_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-C_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(mathcalR',V)ds. This identity holds across all pieces because the intermediate endpoints cancel. N006's H^1 J bound implies each endpoint after P_(>N) has norm <=C_M*N^(-1)*E_I; the initial endpoint is included even when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: Under L1 the displayed two-endpoint normal-form identity holds and its high-output endpoint contribution is <=C_M*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three qualifying paths f1,f2,f3, put Lcut=P_(<=N/3), Hcut=I-Lcut. The trilinear telescoping expansion is C(f1,f2,f3)-C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Lcut f3)=C(Hcut f1,f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Hcut f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Hcut f3). The all-low product has no output above N. Projections contract both parts of X, while ||Hcut fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||fj||_2. In each expanded term apply N002 with the negative norm on its specified high input. Hence ||P_(>N)C_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product||fj||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product||fj||_(L^infty L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e). N009 yields ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I) and bounds the other X norms by C_M; the product of L^2 norms contains E_I. Their total is therefore <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1 the two high-output cubic terms in F002 are bounded by C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

argument.text: For the forcing term, on each intersected step use the actual residual formula N007: integral J(mathcalR',V)=-C(Y_n,z_n,V)-C(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J(W_n,V). The intervals here are the completed or partial intersection with the step. The first two are O_M(tau*q_n) by N002, putting its negative norm on Y_n, using N008's ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q_n and ||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, and N009's bounded V norm on the intersection. The quadratic-in-q term obeys q_n^2<=2*q_n. The last term is O_M(tau*q_n) by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and the L^2 J bound from N006, since the intersection length is <=tau. Every intersected step starts in I, so delta_n<=E_I. There are at most h/tau+1 such steps. Summing bounds the entire forcing term, also after P_(>N), by C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1 the high-output forcing term in F002 has norm <=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Combining F002-F004 gives sup||P_(>N)Fint||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Use F001's low estimate and exact error identity, and N009's accumulated residual estimate, then take the time supremum. This gives E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All estimates were uniform for partial final steps. Discharge L1 and quantify, obtaining N010.

locals.declaration: Fix q as specified in this proof.
Fix L as specified in this proof.
Set tau=T/L.
Set M=1+A(T,gamma,R), using the uniform bound in N001.
Let K0>=1 dominate the constant C_M in N010 for the uniform M.
Choose N>=2 large enough that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4.
Set Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta)+1 and K=max(1,2*K0*delta*(2^Bcount-1)); enlarge if needed for the uniform local constant.
Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma)).

argument.text: H001-H003 fix T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. By N001 choose the common exact-solution bound M=1+A(T,gamma,R); it is independent of the datum in the ball. Let K0>=1 dominate the constant in N010 for this M. For an arbitrary smooth real mean-zero q in that ball and any positive integer L, N007 gives a global smooth finite-step trajectory and continuous interpolation. N001 gives the smooth exact solution, so e=v-V is continuous, starts at zero, and exists on the full interval. The constants M,K0 are chosen before q and L and involve no higher Sobolev norm. In what follows the only temporary restriction on error size is the bootstrap used to invoke N010.

produces.statement: There are common constants M,K0 depending only on T,gamma,R, and every smooth-data finite-step exact/interpolation error e is continuous with e(0)=0.

argument.text: Choose an integer N>=2 so large that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4; this is possible because pstar>0. Choose delta=min(1,1/[4*K0*(N^2+3)])>0 and restrict tau<=min(1,delta/2). On any grid-start interval with length h<=delta and E_I<=1, the small-frequency and timestep terms obey K0*(N^2*h+h+tau)<=K0*delta*(N^2+3)<=1/4. N010 therefore absorbs at most half of E_I and yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K1*delta*tau^gamma with K1 depending only on K0 (take K1=3*K0). This estimate includes both endpoints and does not require e(a)=0.

produces.statement: For tau<=min(1,delta/2), every grid-start interval of length <=delta with E_I<=1 satisfies E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma.

argument.text: Split the grid into successive blocks of floor(delta/tau) steps, with a possibly shorter last block. The full block lengths lie in [delta/2,delta], so there are at most Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta)+1 blocks, independent of tau. Assuming L1: the bootstrap E<=1 holds on a prefix ending at any time, apply F002 block by block, using a partial final interval if that time is interior to a step. Induction starting at zero gives ||e|| on the first j blocks <=3*K0*delta*(2^j-1)*tau^gamma. Thus on every such prefix sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where choose K=max(1,3*K0*delta*(2^Bcount-1)). Discharge L1 to retain this conditional bound for every bootstrap-valid prefix.

produces.statement: For any prefix with error supremum <=1, sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where K depends only on T,gamma,R and tau<=min(1,delta/2).

argument.text: Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time t*, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,t*]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(t*)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. This proves N011, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.

argument.text: H001-H003 give the fixed admissible T,gamma,R. Choose common C,tau0>0 from N011, depending only on these three. Fix arbitrary u0,L and assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma, ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, L is a positive integer and tau=T/L<=tau0. Set u0m=P_(<=m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and the tail of the convergent weighted square sum shows u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L^2. N001 supplies the exact rough solution u and smooth solutions um with one common M. Its two-flow estimate at B0=2R gives sup_[0,T]||um-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0m-u0||_2->0.

produces.statement: Under L1 smooth initial truncations stay in the same H^gamma ball and um converges to the prescribed exact solution u in C([0,T];L^2).

argument.text: Hold the currently chosen tau>0 and L finite. N007 proves continuity of Psi_tau on mean-zero L^2 directly for the exact unmodified formulas: inverse derivatives enter every nonlinear factor, H^1 products are bounded, P0(f^2) is continuous, and the finite coefficient tau^(-1) causes no problem at fixed tau. Therefore induction on n=0,...,L yields U_m^n->U^n in L^2. The base is u0m->u0; the step follows by applying the continuous Psi_tau. All these iterates are real and mean-zero by N007. This finite-step limit requires no uniform-in-tau stability of the map or numerical Sobolev bound.

argument.text: N011 gives max_(0<=n<=L)||um(t_n)-U_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma with the same C,tau0 for every m. By F001-F002 each error vector converges in L^2; taking the maximum over the finite L+1 grid points and passing to the limit preserves the inequality. N006's unitary S_t and N007's grid matching justify exactly the same grid error used in the twisted smooth argument; no cutoff is introduced in Psi_tau. The limit u has the precise solution convention and distributional equation from N001, on the stated normalized torus. Discharge L1 and quantify u0 and L while retaining C,tau0 chosen first. This proves P, including the full initial-ball uniformity, gamma=1 endpoint, and independence of Fourier support.

spec.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u and the fixed unfiltered scheme U defined below satisfy max_{0<=n<=L} ||u(n*tau)-U^n||_2 <= C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. Both constants are uniform over the entire initial-data ball, all such L, and Fourier support.

definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

definitions.type: family of real or complex Hilbert spaces indexed by real order
definitions.definition: Write <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_{k in Z}<k>^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2, interpreted as distributions for s<0. L^2=H^0 and ||.||_2 denotes its normalized norm. For mean-zero f, ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2. For s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s). In time L^infty norms are essential suprema, replaced by ordinary suprema for continuous representatives; derivative norms remain essential suprema.

P0 f=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at zero. Write Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). Spatial differentiation partial_x has multiplier i*k.

definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, define Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2]. Define Htau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). For a positive integer L, tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau; U^0=u0, U^(n+1)=Psi_tau(U^n), 0<=n<L. This is the unmodified scheme with no frequency cutoff. Its elementary L^2 well-definedness and continuity are proved below.
For real K>=0, P_(<=K) has multiplier 1_(|k|<=K) and P_(>K)=I-P_(<=K). These are proof devices and are absent from Scheme.

definitions.type: averaged covariance of two real phases
definitions.definition: For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
For integers a,b,c and k=a+b+c, set p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3.

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, resolving ties in any order. Nthird(a,b,c,d)=N3. Thus N3 is the second smallest of all four magnitudes including the dual output.

definitions.definition: For tau>0, real base time t_n and k!=0, hat R2_(t_n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)(k)=-(tau/(18*i*k))*sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0}exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with zero coefficient at k=0; Phase gives alpha,beta,Phi. pstar=23/14.

J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For I=[a,b], C_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt. Constant inputs are identified with constant time paths. At smooth inputs this is an ordinary integral, and the source estimates supply its continuous extensions.

definitions.definition: For an interval I, ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infty(I;L^2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-pstar))). Use the continuous L^2 representative wherever supplied.

definitions.type: family of bilinear integrated quadratic stages
definitions.definition: For a base time a>=0, step tau>0, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero inputs f,g, F_a(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(f,g)ds. Abbreviate F_a(t;f)=F_a(t;f,f). Its endpoint representation and extensions are proved below.

definitions.type: distributional evolution equation and smooth-approximation solution convention
definitions.definition: KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0, with real mean-zero data on Torus. An exact solution at regularity sigma>=0 means its unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^sigma) distributional solution obtained as the limit of smooth-data solutions. This convention alone grants neither existence nor a bound; these are proved from the registered flow source. For an existing solution write its twisted path v(t)=S_(-t)u(t).

definitions.type: stepwise interpolation and residual construction from a smooth trajectory
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t_n=n*tau, and a finite smooth mean-zero trajectory f_n, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put F_n(t)=F_(t_n)(t;f_n,f_n), z_n=f_n+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f_n,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n, and Y_n=V-z_n. Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n. The residual path mathcalR is the concatenation of these increments: mathcalR(0)=0 and mathcalR(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. This construction does not assert endpoint compatibility; that is proved when f_n are the twisted Scheme trajectory.

propositions.statement: Source flow assertions on the normalized 2*pi torus, in mean-zero homogeneous spaces: for real mean-zero initial datum q, define U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx and its twist y_k(t)=exp(i*t*k^3)hat U(t,k), satisfying y'_k=(i*k/2)sum_{r+s=k}exp(3*i*k*r*s*t)y_r*y_s. (i) For sigma>=0, horizon b>0, and ||q||_2<=B0, the Galerkin approximations with nonlinearity projected onto |k|<=m are uniformly bounded in L^infty([0,b];dot H^sigma) by A_sigma depending only on sigma,b,B0,||q||_(dot H^sigma) (bound clause of Theorem 4.2). (ii) If sigma>0 and 0<rho<sigma, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];H^rho), every fixed 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infty dot H^sigma to a coefficientwise integral solution with the same bound and ||y(t)||_2=||q||_2 a.e. (Theorem 4.3). (iii) That solution is unique, is in C([0,b];dot H^sigma), conserves L^2 for every time, and depends Lipschitz continuously on initial data in dot H^sigma: for sigma>1/2 the constant may depend on sigma,b and the two initial dot H^sigma norms; for 0<sigma<=1/2 the continuity and uniqueness assertions hold as in Theorem 6.3. For sigma=0 there is a unique C([0,b];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation, Lipschitz in its data (Theorems 5.1,6.3,6.4). (iv) For -1<theta<=0, any two such flows whose initial L^2 norms sum to at most B0 satisfy sup_[0,b]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^b*||y(0)-z(0)||_(dot H^theta) (Theorem 6.5). The same norm statements hold for U by the Fourier twist.

propositions.statement: For every real mean-zero q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R, KdV has the exact solution prescribed in D020; it belongs to C([0,T];H^gamma), and sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity uniformly in q. For smooth q the solution is smooth. The twist v=S_(-t)u has the same norms and satisfies v'=B_t(v,v)/2. For any two such solutions with initial L^2 norms summing to at most B0, sup_[0,T]||u-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-qtilde||_2. In particular smooth approximations with bounded H^gamma norm converge in C([0,T];L^2); M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma) is bounded by 1+A(T,gamma,R).
