argument.text: H001-H003 fix T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. By N001 choose the common exact-solution bound M=1+A(T,gamma,R); it is independent of the datum in the ball. Let K0>=1 dominate the constant in N010 for this M. For an arbitrary smooth real mean-zero q in that ball and any positive integer L, N007 gives a global smooth finite-step trajectory and continuous interpolation. N001 gives the smooth exact solution, so e=v-V is continuous, starts at zero, and exists on the full interval. The constants M,K0 are chosen before q and L and involve no higher Sobolev norm. In what follows the only temporary restriction on error size is the bootstrap used to invoke N010.

produces.statement: There are common constants M,K0 depending only on T,gamma,R, and every smooth-data finite-step exact/interpolation error e is continuous with e(0)=0.

argument.text: Choose an integer N>=2 so large that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4; this is possible because pstar>0. Choose delta=min(1,1/[4*K0*(N^2+3)])>0 and restrict tau<=min(1,delta/2). On any grid-start interval with length h<=delta and E_I<=1, the small-frequency and timestep terms obey K0*(N^2*h+h+tau)<=K0*delta*(N^2+3)<=1/4. N010 therefore absorbs at most half of E_I and yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K1*delta*tau^gamma with K1 depending only on K0 (take K1=3*K0). This estimate includes both endpoints and does not require e(a)=0.

produces.statement: For tau<=min(1,delta/2), every grid-start interval of length <=delta with E_I<=1 satisfies E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma.

argument.text: Split the grid into successive blocks of floor(delta/tau) steps, with a possibly shorter last block. The full block lengths lie in [delta/2,delta], so there are at most Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta)+1 blocks, independent of tau. Assuming L1: the bootstrap E<=1 holds on a prefix ending at any time, apply F002 block by block, using a partial final interval if that time is interior to a step. Induction starting at zero gives ||e|| on the first j blocks <=3*K0*delta*(2^j-1)*tau^gamma. Thus on every such prefix sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where choose K=max(1,3*K0*delta*(2^Bcount-1)). Discharge L1 to retain this conditional bound for every bootstrap-valid prefix.

produces.statement: For any prefix with error supremum <=1, sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where K depends only on T,gamma,R and tau<=min(1,delta/2).

argument.text: Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time t*, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,t*]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(t*)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. This proves N011, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.

argument.text: H001-H003 give the fixed admissible T,gamma,R. Choose common C,tau0>0 from N011, depending only on these three. Fix arbitrary u0,L and assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma, ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, L is a positive integer and tau=T/L<=tau0. Set u0m=P_(<=m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and the tail of the convergent weighted square sum shows u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L^2. N001 supplies the exact rough solution u and smooth solutions um with one common M. Its two-flow estimate at B0=2R gives sup_[0,T]||um-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0m-u0||_2->0.

produces.statement: Under L1 smooth initial truncations stay in the same H^gamma ball and um converges to the prescribed exact solution u in C([0,T];L^2).

argument.text: Hold the currently chosen tau>0 and L finite. N007 proves continuity of Psi_tau on mean-zero L^2 directly for the exact unmodified formulas: inverse derivatives enter every nonlinear factor, H^1 products are bounded, P0(f^2) is continuous, and the finite coefficient tau^(-1) causes no problem at fixed tau. Therefore induction on n=0,...,L yields U_m^n->U^n in L^2. The base is u0m->u0; the step follows by applying the continuous Psi_tau. All these iterates are real and mean-zero by N007. This finite-step limit requires no uniform-in-tau stability of the map or numerical Sobolev bound.

produces.statement: Under L1, for the fixed tau and finite L, max_(0<=n<=L)||U_m^n-U^n||_2 tends to zero.

argument.text: N011 gives max_(0<=n<=L)||um(t_n)-U_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma with the same C,tau0 for every m. By F001-F002 each error vector converges in L^2; taking the maximum over the finite L+1 grid points and passing to the limit preserves the inequality. N006's unitary S_t and N007's grid matching justify exactly the same grid error used in the twisted smooth argument; no cutoff is introduced in Psi_tau. The limit u has the precise solution convention and distributional equation from N001, on the stated normalized torus. Discharge L1 and quantify u0 and L while retaining C,tau0 chosen first. 22: author inspection groups and mathematical audit checks. The clean author and

24: self-containment documents supply schemas and detailed meanings; they do not
25: expand the trusted elementary layer.

28: and [tool template](../templates/authoring.md). Build the actual proof,
29: declarations, source contracts and input/output interfaces together. Preserve
30: routine completion and substantive-gap handling in that guide.
31: 
32: At release, inspect the stored own packets and report actual readiness. Keep
33: known unresolved findings open until their located correction or justified
34: withdrawal. Complete notes alone do not finish authoring. An unfinished draft
35: is preserved as unfinished, without an ordinary first-acceptance audit.
36: 
37: The auditor separately performs the execution protocol in Audit A: source
38: verification, global review, fresh packet-only replay, actual judgments and
39: recorded evidence. Authors do not generate those verdicts. The NL0 author and
40: global Audit A are serial. After the global stage, independent frozen R packets
41: are reviewed with the confirmed N workers. Separate cases can run concurrently.

44: 
45: Keep `spec.json` independent of the authoring file. The canonical proof is
46: `nl0.json`; `NL0.md` and `graph.mmd` are generated views. Do not edit the views
47: as mathematical authorities.

54: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py check PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --audit PATH/audit-a.json
55: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py inspect-audit PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --audit PATH/audit-a.json
56: ```

59: successfully validate the completeness of a FAIL/UNVERIFIED record; its
60: `audit_receipt_valid` remains false and it is never an acceptance command.

62: and exact meaning of the checks are documented in the data contract. Programs
63: validate explicit metadata and evidence binding; they cannot recognize every
64: undeclared theorem or prove a natural-language argument.
65:

67: A detailed-NL0 audit v3 does not establish current format-4 acceptance. Historical v1 files
68: require explicit `--legacy`; their receipts cannot establish current-standard
69: acceptance. Do not silently migrate, overwrite, or relabel old cases. The
70: archived case-2 authoring script no longer manufactures passing reviews.

72: example with an unperformed audit, not a new benchmark or certification.

75: 
76: - `STRUCTURE-PASSED`: schema, graph, explicit references, frozen specification,
77:   and definition prerequisites passed the mechanical checks.
78: - `AUDIT-RECEIPT-VALID`: a complete, matching audit record was checked. This is
79:   an evidence/coverage verdict, not the program proving the mathematics.
80: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED`: the named auditor actually completed Audit A for every
81:   source, definition, inference, and target obligation. Report whether the
82:   auditor shared context with the author; never relabel self-audit as an
83:   independent review or Lean verification.
84: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-CONDITIONAL`: complete review relative to explicit external
85:   statements whose primary sources remain unverified. Preserve the source
86:   warnings and follow the [conditional-source policy](conditional-sources.md).
87: - `GAP`, `SOURCE-MISMATCH`, `TARGET-MISMATCH`, `ASSUMPTION-MISMATCH`, `INVALID`,
88:   or `UNVERIFIED`: identify the exact failing obligation and affected closure.

91: Changed claims, inputs, arguments, definitions, assumptions, or sources revoke
92: the affected verdicts. Reuse is limited to previously qualified unchanged items
93: whose current content, dependencies, review scope and evidence bindings still
94: verify. Changed or newly required items need actual review; missing or stale
95: evidence cannot grant acceptance. Preserve the earlier findings and failed
96: reports. Never add the missing conclusion as an H, source theorem, definition
97: property, structure field, or typeclass merely to close the graph.

100:

102: diagram, primary-source/signature evidence, per-object Audit A, mechanical
103: results, and the first remaining gap. Describe functional smoke tests and
104: negative controls separately from mathematical review, isolation, formalization,
105: and speed experiments. Graph construction and auditing time are real costs.
106: Explicitly notify the user of every citation check deferred for inaccessible
107: primary text, including the affected E IDs, attempted retrieval routes and
108: remaining verification needs. Do not describe a partial audit as fully passed."}

item.name: exec

value.statement: There is an absolute C such that for every finite-support nonnegative ell^2 quadruple y1,y2,y3,y4, sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0)y1(a)y2(b)y3(c)y4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_(j=1)^4||yj||_ell2.

For every contributing nonzero frequency triple r1,r2,r3 with k0=r1+r2+r3!=0 and r1+r2!=0, and phases alpha0=3*r1*r2*(r1+r2), beta0=3*k0*r3*(r1+r2), one has |eta_tau(alpha0,beta0)|/(|k0|*|r1*r2*r3|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird(r1,r2,r3,-k0).

patches.value: For 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, any real base time a, and mean-zero fj in H^sigma, ||R2_(a,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly in a,tau and Fourier support. The bound holds after inserting any multiplier of modulus <=1, including restriction to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. Polynomial approximation defines its unique continuous trilinear extension. Moreover, for 0<gamma<=1, mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f in mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(a,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). This estimate requires no H^gamma bound on f.

For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. H^1 is an algebra: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

Now fix arbitrary continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b] and a third such path h. On k!=0 the coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(r+s=k)exp(-3*i*k*r*s*t)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiation of the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients, so d_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smoothness gives absolute Fourier convergence for every derivative used. Integrate and divide by three to obtain the normal form, summing over pieces if necessary; continuity makes the internal endpoints cancel. Symmetry is immediate. Because Dinv partial_x=P and S_t commutes with these Fourier multipliers, J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}. Integrating gives C_I(f,g,h) with no commutation through a product. At constant f,g the derivative terms vanish, giving Stage=[J]_a^t/6. Quantifying the inputs proves the asserted conclusion.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau from Scheme is a continuous polynomial map from mean-zero L^2 to mean-zero L^2, preserving reality; Ftau maps L^2 continuously to H^1. Smooth data produce smooth iterates. For any trajectory produced by Scheme from smooth mean-zero data, f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, the Interp construction has V(t_n)=f_n, V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), is continuous and piecewise smooth in time and spatially smooth, and has mean-zero values, which are real whenever the initial datum is real. On each open step, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+mathcalR', where mathcalR'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. Thus mathcalR is continuous with the defining increments and the displayed residual identity holds a.e.
periodic input function; smooth in the second paragraph's source application
For every smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), where f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n. Its exact twisted update is f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n).

value.statement: For every smooth exact path u with v=S_(-t)u and smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, if 0<tau<=1 and M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), then every step index j0 with d0=||f_(j0)-v(t_(j0))||_2<=1 satisfies sup_(I_(j0))||rho_(j0)||_2<=C_M*tau*(tau^gamma+d0) and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_(j0);H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+d0).

patches.value: For the forcing term, on each intersected step use the actual residual formula N007: integral J(mathcalR',V)=-C(Y_n,z_n,V)-C(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J(W_n,V). The intervals here are the completed or partial intersection with the step. The first two are O_M(tau*q_n) by N002, putting its negative norm on Y_n, using N008's ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q_n and ||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, and N009's bounded V norm on the intersection. H002 and 0<tau<=1 give tau^gamma<=1; since delta_n<=E_I<=1, q_n<=2 and q_n^2<=2*q_n. The last term is O_M(tau*q_n) by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and the L^2 J bound from N006, since the intersection length is <=tau. Every intersected step starts in I, so delta_n<=E_I. There are at most h/tau+1 such steps. Summing bounds the entire forcing term, also after P_(>N), by C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).
Set Hcut=identity-Lcut, where identity is the identity Fourier operator.

For any three qualifying paths f1,f2,f3, put Lcut=P_(<=N/3), Hcut=identity-Lcut. The trilinear telescoping expansion is C(f1,f2,f3)-C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Lcut f3)=C(Hcut f1,f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Hcut f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Hcut f3). The all-low product has no output above N. Projections contract both parts of X, while ||Hcut fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||fj||_2. In each expanded term apply N002 with the negative norm on its specified high input. Hence ||P_(>N)C_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product||fj||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product||fj||_(L^infty L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e). N009 yields ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I) and bounds the other X norms by C_M; the product of L^2 norms contains E_I. Their total is therefore <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

Choose an integer N>=2 so large that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4; this is possible because pstar>0. Choose delta=min(1,1/[4*K0*(N^2+3)])>0 and restrict tau<=min(1,delta/2). On any grid-start interval with length h<=delta and E_I<=1, the small-frequency and timestep terms obey K0*(N^2*h+h+tau)<=K0*delta*(N^2+3)<=1/4. N010 therefore absorbs at most half of E_I and yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma. This estimate includes both endpoints and does not require e(a)=0.

Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. Assume L4: tau<=tau0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time tstar, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,tstar]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(tstar)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. Discharge L4 and L3; this proves the smooth-data estimate, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.

value.declaration: Under L2 let tstar be the asserted first time with error norm one. If any crossing exists, continuity from e(0)=0 supplies such a time.
Let U be the Scheme trajectory from u0 at step tau.
For each m let Um be the Scheme trajectory from u0m at the same tau; U_m^n denotes its nth term.
Choose the constant in N001's two-flow comparison at initial norm sum bound 2*R.

P=identity-P0, where identity is the identity linear operator.
For real K>=0, P_(<=K) has Fourier multiplier 1_(|k|<=K) and P_(>K)=identity-P_(<=K), with identity the identity operator. These projections are proof devices and are absent from Scheme.

item.name: exec

patches.value: For all I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and h=b-a<=1, all 0<=sigma<=1 and paths f_j in L^infty(I;H^sigma) with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-pstar)), Ctri satisfies ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C*||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))*product_{j!=i}||f_j||_(L^infty L^2), each i=1,2,3. For time-independent inputs, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*h^sigma*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), including sigma=0. For 0<sigma<=1 choose a_sigma=1/2-sigma for sigma<1/2, a_sigma=1/8 for sigma=1/2, a_sigma=0 for sigma>1/2. Then 0<=a_sigma<1, and for every f in H^sigma and g in H^a_sigma, ||fg||_2<=C_sigma||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^a_sigma). For any constant mean-zero w in H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and a>=0, sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^a_sigma)<=C_(M,sigma)*tau^sigma and sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^(1+sigma))<=C_(M,sigma). All these are in the normalized norms, with constants uniform in endpoints and support.

There is an absolute C>0 such that the following bounds hold uniformly in time. For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. For all A,A2 in H^1, the algebra bound is: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

For a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution u on [0,T], twist v=S_(-t)u, and smooth Scheme trajectory f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, suppose M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Then Interp satisfies sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*q_n. On any I=[a,b] contained in [0,T] with a a grid point, h=b-a<=1, define e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2. If E_I<=1 then sup_I||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_M. Intervals may end inside a step; derivative assertions hold a.e. All constants depend only on M,gamma,T and are uniform in n,tau and Fourier support.
Apply at source base t_0=0, stage time s in [0,tau], inputs f=g=S_a w and beta=a_sigma. The displayed Airy-conjugation identity transfers the H^a_sigma bound to F_a(a+s;w,w).

value.bindings: Apply separately at source base t_0=0, stage time s in [0,tau], inputs f=g=S_a w and beta=1+sigma. The source time exponent is zero; the Airy-conjugation identity transfers this H^(1+sigma) estimate to base a.
hypothesis_checks: L1 and the displayed unitary Fourier calculation give 0<sigma<=1, tau>0 and constant mean-zero H^sigma inputs S_a w on [0,tau].
The upper endpoint beta=1+sigma is in [beta0,1+sigma], as verified in F002.

patches.value: Use sigma=gamma, b=T, q_source(x)=-q(-x) and B0=R for the positive-regularity flow and a priori bound.

value.bindings: In the smooth-data clause, take arbitrary higher Sobolev order sigma>gamma, horizon b=T and reflected source datum -q(-x), with B0=R. Uniqueness identifies these higher-order flows with the gamma-order flow.
hypothesis_checks: In this conditional clause q is smooth, real and mean-zero, reflection preserves these properties, and H001 gives T>0.
Smooth q has a finite homogeneous norm at every chosen sigma>gamma>0, so the positive-regularity existence and uniqueness clauses apply.
Its initial L^2 norm is <=R by L1; clause(iv) is not used here.
